# OpenTelemetry GenAI compatibility matrix

<!-- Generated by scripts/otel_genai_matrix.py from otel-genai-matrix.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

**AiEnsured agentest, an Agentic AI Testing platform** judges what an agent did from its OpenTelemetry traces. The OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions are in *Development* status and change often, so this page lists, for one pinned version of them, what agentest reads, what it reads only in part, and what it does not read.

```bash
pip install agentest-ai
```

Nothing here is an endorsement by OpenTelemetry or by any framework; it is a statement about what agentest's importer does.

## What this page is pinned to

- GenAI conventions repository: <https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai>
- Commit: `81b5d438519f868a186bff088d9de24aefdb2f6b` (a checkout of the model at this commit is what `--semconv-dir` verifies the rows against)
- Release tag at or before that commit: `v0.1.0`
- Schema version agentest declares and reports: `1.42.0` (`https://opentelemetry.io/schemas/1.42.0`); traces that declare an older version are mapped onto the current names (see [Earlier conventions](#earlier-conventions-mapped-onto-the-current-names)).
- Stability of every attribute in the pinned model: Development.

## How to read the table

- **read**: the importer maps the item into the run and at least one of the 130 default checks uses it, or the importer relies on it to structure the run.
- **partial**: read only in some forms or positions, or used only by opt-in rules.
- **not read**: no check interprets it. Every span attribute value still counts toward the leak scans, whether or not the row says *read*.
- **Checks**: the default checks that use the item, from `scripts/rule_fields.py` (the 130 default IDs only; opt-in packs and new tests are not counted unless the row says so).

| Kind | Rows | read | partial | not read |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Operations | 21 | 5 | 3 | 13 |
| Span types | 18 | 4 | 6 | 8 |
| Events | 11 | 1 | 1 | 9 |
| Message parts | 12 | 3 | 3 | 6 |
| Attributes | 97 | 12 | 3 | 82 |
| Metrics | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 |
| **All** | **160** | **25** | **16** | **119** |

## Operations (`gen_ai.operation.name`)

| Name | Status | What agentest does | Checks |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chat` | read | Model call: its output feeds the per-response tool-call batches and step counts. | T2-009, X-005, X-019, X-020 |
| `generate_content` | read | Model call, read like `chat`. | T2-009, X-005, X-019, X-020 |
| `realtime_inference` | read | Model call, read like `chat` (new since 3.7.0). | T2-009, X-005, X-019, X-020 |
| `user_speech` | not read | Kept in the span tree only. | - |
| `text_completion` | read | Model call, read like `chat`. | T2-009, X-005, X-019, X-020 |
| `embeddings` | not read | Kept in the span tree only. | - |
| `retrieval` | not read | Kept in the span tree only. | - |
| `fetch_response` | not read | Not a model call; no content to judge. | - |
| `create_agent` | not read | Agent creation is not a run step. | - |
| `invoke_agent` | partial | Read as the root span or as an agent span in the tree (agent name, turn markers); a handoff needs `agentest.handoff.source`, or a transfer tool span. | T3-002, T3-007, T3-009, T3-011, X-005 |
| `execute_tool` | read | A tool call: name, id, arguments, result and error state. | 107 checks ([list](#checks-per-field)) |
| `invoke_workflow` | partial | Read as an ordinary root or nested span; the workflow's name arrives as `gen_ai.agent.name` (the older `gen_ai.workflow.name` is mapped). | - |
| `invoke_runner` | partial | Read as an ordinary root or nested span. | - |
| `plan` | not read | Kept in the span tree; no check reads planning spans. | - |
| `search_memory` | not read | Memory operations are kept in the span tree only. | - |
| `create_memory` | not read | Memory operations are kept in the span tree only. | - |
| `update_memory` | not read | Memory operations are kept in the span tree only. | - |
| `upsert_memory` | not read | Memory operations are kept in the span tree only. | - |
| `delete_memory` | not read | Memory operations are kept in the span tree only. | - |
| `create_memory_store` | not read | Memory operations are kept in the span tree only. | - |

## Earlier conventions mapped onto the current names

`src/agentest/standards/semconv.yaml` holds the tables. A name already present on a span is never overwritten.

| Style | Convention versions | Renamed to the current name |
|---|---|---|
| `otel-genai-1.37+` | 1.37.0, 1.38.0, 1.39.0, 1.40.0, 1.41.0, 1.42.0, genai@ebe3d1f | `gen_ai.workflow.name` → `gen_ai.agent.name`, `gen_ai.usage.cache_creation.input_tokens` → `gen_ai.usage.cache_write.input_tokens` |
| `otel-genai-1.28-1.36` | 1.28.0, 1.29.0, 1.30.0, 1.31.0, 1.32.0, 1.33.0, 1.34.0, 1.35.0, 1.36.0 | `gen_ai.system` → `gen_ai.provider.name` |
| `otel-genai-1.26-1.27` | 1.26.0, 1.27.0 | `gen_ai.system` → `gen_ai.provider.name`, `gen_ai.usage.prompt_tokens` → `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens`, `gen_ai.usage.completion_tokens` → `gen_ai.usage.output_tokens` |

Two other instrumentation styles (not OpenTelemetry versions) are mapped by the same file; see `semconv.yaml`.

## Tested with the official instrumentation

`tests/test_otel_genai_instrumentation.py` emits one run with the OpenTelemetry GenAI instrumentation library (`opentelemetry-util-genai`, pre-release) in all three content-capture modes (`SPAN_ONLY`, `EVENT_ONLY`, `SPAN_AND_EVENT`) and requires the same verdicts as the hand-written trace of the same behaviour. CI installs the library when it can (`pip install --pre opentelemetry-util-genai`) and then fails, rather than skips, if the test does not run.

## Gaps filled since 3.7.0

- Structured tool results (an OTLP key-value list) are kept as JSON text instead of a Python repr; a non-object tool-argument value no longer raises.
- Content recorded on `gen_ai.client.inference.operation.details` (span event or log record) is merged onto its span.
- `gen_ai.execute_tool.transfer` spans (`gen_ai.transfer.target.name`) are read as handoffs.
- `realtime_inference` is read as a model call.
- `gen_ai.workflow.name` and `gen_ai.usage.cache_creation.input_tokens` (names replaced upstream) are mapped to their successors.

## Not covered

- OpenTelemetry metrics and the MCP and A2A semantic-convention pages: agentest judges traces, and reads MCP tool facts from `tools.json`.
- Content stored outside the trace (the `*_ref` attributes): agentest sees only the reference.
- Provider-specific attributes.

## Keeping this page current

```bash
python scripts/otel_genai_matrix.py --check
git clone https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai /tmp/genai && git -C /tmp/genai checkout 81b5d438519f868a186bff088d9de24aefdb2f6b
python scripts/otel_genai_matrix.py --check --semconv-dir /tmp/genai
```

CI runs both. To move the pin, check out the newer commit, run the second command, add or change the rows it reports, update `genai_commit` in `semconv.yaml` and the `commit` in `otel-genai-matrix.json`, then run `--write`.
